sentence_stem: Never before had the team faced such a difficult deadline,
correct_completion: had they been asked to deliver so much in so little time.
full_sentence: Never before had the team faced such a difficult deadline, had they been asked to deliver so much in so little time.
acceptable_variants: never had they been asked to deliver so much in so little time.
rarely had they been given such a demanding task.

options.text: the team had completed the project early.
options.why_wrong: This is a positive statement in normal word order. Negative inversion requires the auxiliary verb to come before the subject after the negative adverb.

options.text: they were asked to deliver so much in so little time.
options.why_wrong: This is a normal word order sentence. After 'never before', the auxiliary 'had' must come before the subject.

options.text: had they been asked to deliver so much in so little time.
they had been asked to deliver so much in so little time.
options.why_wrong: This keeps the normal subject-verb order. The negative adverb 'never before' requires inversion, so 'had' must precede 'they'.

explanation: When a negative adverb such as 'never before' begins a clause, English puts the auxiliary verb before the subject. Learners whose first language does not use this structure often keep the normal order by mistake.
translation: Ніколи раніше команда не стикалася з таким складним терміном, і їх ніколи не просили так багато зробити за такий короткий час.
